items.prompt:
Which of the following is a characteristic shown by all living things?

A) Respiration
B) Rusting
C) Crystallisation
D) Evaporation

The release of energy from food within living cells is known as:

A) Excretion
B) Respiration
C) Reproduction
D) Irritability

The ability of an organism to respond to changes in its environment is called:

A) Reproduction
B) Nutrition
C) Irritability (sensitivity)
D) Growth

The characteristic of living things by which the whole body or its parts change position is:

A) Excretion
B) Nutrition
C) Respiration
D) Movement

The process by which living things obtain and use food is called:

A) Nutrition
B) Excretion
C) Respiration
D) Reproduction

The removal of metabolic waste products from the body of an organism is:

A) Egestion
B) Excretion
C) Secretion
D) Ingestion

An irreversible increase in the size and dry mass of an organism is termed:

A) Movement
B) Respiration
C) Growth
D) Irritability

The life process that ensures the continuity of a species from one generation to the next is:

A) Excretion
B) Nutrition
C) Respiration
D) Reproduction

The basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms is the:

A) Cell
B) Tissue
C) Organ
D) System

A group of similar cells performing the same function is called a:

A) Cell
B) Tissue
C) Organ
D) Organism

Different tissues working together to perform a particular function form an:

A) Tissue
B) Cell
C) Organ
D) Population

A group of organs working together to carry out a major body function is a(n):

A) Tissue
B) Organism
C) Community
D) System

The removal of undigested food materials from the body is correctly called:

A) Egestion
B) Excretion
C) Secretion
D) Respiration

The sum total of all chemical reactions taking place in a living cell is called:

A) Respiration
B) Metabolism
C) Photosynthesis
D) Digestion

mcq_options.text: It carries out respiration and reproduction
It can be moved by wind

items.prompt:
Which feature best distinguishes a living organism from a non-living thing?

A) It has a fixed shape
B) It is made of atoms
C) It carries out respiration and reproduction
D) It can be moved by wind
items.correct_answer: C) It carries out respiration and reproduction

items.prompt:
A complete living thing made up of several systems working together is a(n):

A) Organ
B) Tissue
C) Cell
D) Organism

Which sequence correctly shows increasing complexity of organisation?

A) Cell -> tissue -> organ -> system -> organism
B) Organism -> system -> organ -> tissue -> cell
C) Tissue -> cell -> organ -> system -> organism
D) Organ -> cell -> tissue -> system -> organism
items.correct_answer: A) Cell -> tissue -> organ -> system -> organism

items.prompt:
The gradual adjustment of an organism to suit its environment over time is known as:

A) Excretion
B) Adaptation
C) Irritability
D) Egestion

Carbon dioxide and urea produced inside the body are examples of:

A) Undigested food
B) Nutrients
C) Metabolic waste products
D) Hormones

mcq_options.text: Metabolism such as respiration and nutrition

items.prompt:
A reliable way to confirm that an object was once living is that it once carried out:

A) Reflection of light
B) Dissolving in water
C) Conduction of electricity
D) Metabolism such as respiration and nutrition
items.correct_answer: D) Metabolism such as respiration and nutrition

items.prompt:
Who first observed and named cells while examining a thin slice of cork?

A) Robert Hooke
B) Charles Darwin
C) Gregor Mendel
D) Louis Pasteur

The organelle that controls the activities of the cell and contains genetic material is the:

A) Mitochondrion
B) Nucleus
C) Ribosome
D) Vacuole

The structure that controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell is the:

A) Cell wall
B) Nucleolus
C) Cell membrane
D) Centriole

The organelle described as the powerhouse of the cell because it releases energy is the:

A) Ribosome
B) Golgi body
C) Lysosome
D) Mitochondrion

The green organelle that traps light energy for photosynthesis is the:

A) Chloroplast
B) Mitochondrion
C) Nucleus
D) Vacuole

The site of protein synthesis within the cell is the:

A) Lysosome
B) Ribosome
C) Centriole
D) Vacuole

A rigid structure made of cellulose found outside the membrane of plant cells is the:

A) Cell membrane
B) Plasma layer
C) Cell wall
D) Cuticle

The large fluid-filled organelle that helps maintain turgidity in plant cells is the:

A) Nucleus
B) Ribosome
C) Mitochondrion
D) Vacuole

Which structure is found in plant cells but absent in typical animal cells?

A) Cell wall
B) Nucleus
C) Cell membrane
D) Cytoplasm

The jelly-like medium in which the cell organelles are suspended is the:

A) Nucleoplasm
B) Cytoplasm
C) Vacuole
D) Cell sap

The organelle that contains digestive enzymes and breaks down worn-out structures is the:

A) Ribosome
B) Chloroplast
C) Lysosome
D) Centriole

The organelle that packages and secretes cell products is the:

A) Mitochondrion
B) Nucleus
C) Vacuole
D) Golgi apparatus

The green pigment found inside chloroplasts that absorbs light is:

A) Chlorophyll
B) Haemoglobin
C) Melanin
D) Carotene

The structure that separates the nucleus from the cytoplasm is the:

A) Cell wall
B) Nuclear membrane
C) Plasma membrane
D) Tonoplast

An organism made up of only one cell, such as Amoeba, is described as:

A) Multicellular
B) Acellular
C) Unicellular
D) Colonial

The network of membranes that transports materials within the cell is the:

A) Endoplasmic reticulum
B) Golgi body
C) Cell wall
D) Nucleolus

mcq_options.text: Cells arise only from non-living matter
All living things are made of one or more cells
Only plants are made of cells
Cells have no role in heredity

items.prompt:
Which statement is part of the modern cell theory?

A) Cells arise only from non-living matter
B) All living things are made of one or more cells
C) Only plants are made of cells
D) Cells have no role in heredity
items.correct_answer: B) All living things are made of one or more cells

items.prompt:
The combined action of the cell wall and a full vacuole keeps a plant cell:

A) Flabby and plasmolysed
B) Dead and dry
C) Firm and turgid
D) Colourless

mcq_options.text: Require large amounts of energy for contraction

items.prompt:
An organism's muscle cells contain very many mitochondria mainly because they:

A) Need to store starch
B) Carry out photosynthesis
C) Make their own light
D) Require large amounts of energy for contraction
items.correct_answer: D) Require large amounts of energy for contraction

items.prompt:
Cell division that produces two daughter cells identical to the parent cell is:

A) Mitosis
B) Meiosis
C) Fertilisation
D) Budding

The thread-like structures in the nucleus that carry hereditary information are:

A) Ribosomes
B) Chromosomes
C) Centrioles
D) Vacuoles

Cell division that halves the chromosome number and forms gametes is:

A) Mitosis
B) Binary fission
C) Meiosis
D) Regeneration

mcq_options.text: Half that of the parent cell
Double that of the parent cell
The same as the parent cell

items.prompt:
At the end of mitosis, each daughter cell has a chromosome number that is:

A) Half that of the parent cell
B) Double that of the parent cell
C) Always zero
D) The same as the parent cell
items.correct_answer: D) The same as the parent cell

mcq_options.text: Half that of the parent cell
Double that of the parent cell

items.prompt:
Gametes formed by meiosis contain a chromosome number that is:

A) Half that of the parent cell
B) Equal to the parent cell
C) Double that of the parent cell
D) Always 46
items.correct_answer: A) Half that of the parent cell

items.prompt:
Mitosis is important in living organisms mainly for:

A) Formation of gametes only
B) Growth and repair of tissues
C) Reducing chromosome number
D) Producing genetic variation
items.correct_answer: B) Growth and repair of tissues

mcq_options.text: Maintains a constant chromosome number across generations

items.prompt:
A major importance of meiosis is that it:

A) Repairs damaged skin
B) Heals wounds
C) Maintains a constant chromosome number across generations
D) Produces identical body cells
items.correct_answer: C) Maintains a constant chromosome number across generations

items.prompt:
A cell containing two complete sets of chromosomes is described as:

A) Haploid
B) Triploid
C) Aneuploid
D) Diploid

A gamete that contains only one set of chromosomes is said to be:

A) Haploid
B) Diploid
C) Polyploid
D) Tetraploid

The normal number of chromosomes in a human body cell is:

A) 23
B) 46
C) 92
D) 48

Before division, a cell copies its DNA during a stage called:

A) Anaphase
B) Telophase
C) Interphase
D) Cytokinesis

mcq_options.text: Crossing over and random assortment of chromosomes

items.prompt:
Meiosis contributes to variation among offspring mainly through:

A) Exact copying of all genes
B) Loss of all chromosomes
C) Doubling of chromosome number
D) Crossing over and random assortment of chromosomes
items.correct_answer: D) Crossing over and random assortment of chromosomes

items.prompt:
The division of the cytoplasm that follows nuclear division is called:

A) Cytokinesis
B) Karyokinesis
C) Interphase
D) Synapsis

The region where two sister chromatids of a chromosome are joined is the:

A) Telomere
B) Centromere
C) Centriole
D) Spindle

Sex cells such as sperm and ova, produced by meiosis, are called:

A) Zygotes
B) Somatic cells
C) Gametes
D) Spores

After fertilisation, the zygote develops into an embryo mainly by:

A) Meiosis
B) Binary fission
C) Budding
D) Repeated mitosis

The exchange of segments between homologous chromosomes during meiosis is:

A) Crossing over
B) Translocation
C) Cytokinesis
D) Replication

Which type of cell normally divides by mitosis in the human body?

A) Sperm-forming cells producing gametes
B) Skin (body) cells
C) Egg-forming cells producing gametes
D) Pollen mother cells

Each of the two identical copies of a chromosome formed after DNA replication is a:

A) Centromere
B) Gene
C) Chromatid
D) Allele

Fusion of two haploid gametes at fertilisation restores the:

A) Haploid chromosome number
B) Triploid chromosome number
C) Zero chromosome number
D) Diploid chromosome number

Organisms that manufacture their own food from simple inorganic substances are:

A) Autotrophs
B) Heterotrophs
C) Saprophytes
D) Parasites

Organisms that obtain their food from other organisms are described as:

A) Autotrophs
B) Heterotrophs
C) Producers
D) Phototrophs

Biological catalysts that speed up reactions in living cells are called:

A) Hormones
B) Vitamins
C) Enzymes
D) Substrates

The mode of nutrition in which animals take in solid food, digest and absorb it is:

A) Saprophytic nutrition
B) Parasitic nutrition
C) Autotrophic nutrition
D) Holozoic nutrition

An organism such as a mushroom that feeds on dead organic matter is a:

A) Saprophyte
B) Parasite
C) Producer
D) Predator

An organism that lives on or in another living organism and harms it is a:

A) Saprophyte
B) Parasite
C) Host
D) Symbiont

Enzymes are chemically classified as:

A) Fats
B) Carbohydrates
C) Proteins
D) Mineral salts

The enzyme in saliva that begins the digestion of starch is:

A) Pepsin
B) Trypsin
C) Lipase
D) Amylase (ptyalin)

The enzyme that digests protein in the acidic stomach is:

A) Pepsin
B) Amylase
C) Lipase
D) Maltase

The enzyme that breaks fats down into fatty acids and glycerol is:

A) Pepsin
B) Lipase
C) Amylase
D) Trypsin

mcq_options.text: Able to act on any substance

items.prompt:
A key property of enzymes is that each enzyme is:

A) Able to act on any substance
B) Used up in every reaction
C) Specific to a particular substrate
D) Made of carbohydrate
items.correct_answer: C) Specific to a particular substrate

items.prompt:
Most human enzymes work best at a temperature of about:

A) 0 degrees Celsius
B) 100 degrees Celsius
C) 5 degrees Celsius
D) 37 degrees Celsius

When an enzyme is destroyed by high temperature it is said to be:

A) Denatured
B) Activated
C) Catalysed
D) Hydrolysed

Green plants absorb nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium from the soil as:

A) Vitamins
B) Mineral salts
C) Proteins
D) Enzymes

A close association between two organisms in which both benefit is called:

A) Parasitism
B) Predation
C) Symbiosis (mutualism)
D) Commensalism

A green plant such as the sundew that traps insects for nitrogen is described as:

A) Saprophytic plant
B) Parasitic plant
C) Epiphytic plant
D) Insectivorous (carnivorous) plant

Pepsin works best in the stomach because the conditions there are:

A) Acidic
B) Strongly alkaline
C) Neutral
D) Salt-free

mcq_options.text: Are destroyed in every reaction they catalyse
Speed up reactions without being used up
Are made fresh for each molecule

items.prompt:
Enzymes are described as catalysts because they:

A) Are destroyed in every reaction they catalyse
B) Speed up reactions without being used up
C) Supply energy to the reaction
D) Are made fresh for each molecule
items.correct_answer: B) Speed up reactions without being used up

items.prompt:
A diet containing carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, mineral salts, water and roughage is described as:

A) A carbohydrate diet
B) A protein diet
C) A balanced diet
D) A starvation diet

The indigestible plant fibre that adds bulk to food and prevents constipation is:

A) Glucose
B) Protein
C) Vitamin C
D) Roughage (dietary fibre)

The process by which green plants make food using light energy is called:

A) Photosynthesis
B) Respiration
C) Transpiration
D) Digestion

The two raw materials needed for photosynthesis are:

A) Oxygen and glucose
B) Carbon dioxide and water
C) Nitrogen and water
D) Oxygen and carbon dioxide

The main food substance produced during photosynthesis is:

A) Protein
B) Fat
C) Glucose (carbohydrate)
D) Urea

The gas released into the air during photosynthesis is:

A) Carbon dioxide
B) Nitrogen
C) Hydrogen
D) Oxygen

The pigment that traps light energy for photosynthesis is:

A) Chlorophyll
B) Haemoglobin
C) Melanin
D) Xanthophyll

Photosynthesis takes place mainly in the cell organelle called the:

A) Mitochondrion
B) Chloroplast
C) Nucleus
D) Ribosome

The source of energy for photosynthesis is:

A) Heat from the soil
B) Chemical energy from glucose
C) Sunlight
D) Energy from wind

The chemical used to test a leaf for the presence of starch is:

A) Limewater
B) Benedict's solution
C) Sodium hydroxide
D) Iodine solution

When starch is present in a tested leaf, iodine solution turns:

A) Blue-black
B) Brick-red
C) Milky white
D) Colourless

mcq_options.text: Add more starch to the leaf

items.prompt:
Leaving a plant in the dark before a starch test is done in order to:

A) Add more starch to the leaf
B) Remove starch already present (destarch it)
C) Kill the plant
D) Warm up the leaf
items.correct_answer: B) Remove starch already present (destarch it)

items.prompt:
A leaf is boiled in alcohol during the starch test mainly to:

A) Add starch
B) Kill insects
C) Remove the chlorophyll
D) Add iodine

Carbon dioxide enters the leaf for photosynthesis mainly through the:

A) Cuticle
B) Xylem
C) Root hairs
D) Stomata

Which word equation correctly summarises photosynthesis?

A) Carbon dioxide + water -> glucose + oxygen
B) Glucose + oxygen -> carbon dioxide + water
C) Glucose -> carbon dioxide + alcohol
D) Water + oxygen -> glucose + carbon dioxide
items.correct_answer: A) Carbon dioxide + water -> glucose + oxygen

items.prompt:
Photosynthesis is important to life on earth because it:

A) Uses up all the oxygen
B) Produces food and releases oxygen
C) Removes all carbon dioxide forever
D) Destroys green plants
items.correct_answer: B) Produces food and releases oxygen

items.prompt:
Which of the following is a factor that can limit the rate of photosynthesis?

A) Soil colour
B) Wind direction
C) Light intensity
D) Air pressure only

Excess glucose made during photosynthesis is usually stored in the leaf as:

A) Protein
B) Glycogen
C) Fat
D) Starch

In a variegated leaf, only the green parts make starch because the white parts lack:

A) Chlorophyll
B) Water
C) Carbon dioxide
D) Stomata

mcq_options.text: Absorb carbon dioxide from the air around the leaf

items.prompt:
Soda lime is placed in an experiment on photosynthesis in order to:

A) Supply extra carbon dioxide
B) Absorb carbon dioxide from the air around the leaf
C) Add water vapour
D) Provide light
items.correct_answer: B) Absorb carbon dioxide from the air around the leaf

items.prompt:
At dawn there is a light level at which photosynthesis just balances respiration; this is the:

A) Saturation point
B) Wilting point
C) Compensation point
D) Boiling point

During photosynthesis, light energy is converted into:

A) Heat energy only
B) Sound energy
C) Electrical energy
D) Chemical energy stored in glucose
items.correct_answer: D) Chemical energy stored in glucose

items.prompt:
The plant tissue that conducts water and mineral salts upward from the roots is the:

A) Xylem
B) Phloem
C) Cambium
D) Cortex

The plant tissue that transports manufactured food from the leaves is the:

A) Xylem
B) Phloem
C) Epidermis
D) Pith

The fluid tissue that transports materials around the human body is:

A) Lymph only
B) Bile
C) Blood
D) Urine

The blood cells that carry oxygen by means of haemoglobin are the:

A) White blood cells
B) Platelets
C) Plasma
D) Red blood cells

The blood cells that defend the body against disease are the:

A) White blood cells
B) Red blood cells
C) Platelets
D) Lymph cells only

The pale yellow fluid part of blood in which cells are suspended is:

A) Serum only
B) Lymph
C) Plasma
D) Bile

The red pigment in red blood cells that combines with oxygen is:

A) Chlorophyll
B) Melanin
C) Fibrinogen
D) Haemoglobin

Blood vessels that carry blood away from the heart are called:

A) Arteries
B) Veins
C) Capillaries
D) Lymphatics

Blood vessels that return blood to the heart and have valves are:

A) Arteries
B) Veins
C) Capillaries
D) Arterioles

The tiny vessels where exchange of materials between blood and tissues occurs are:

A) Arteries
B) Veins
C) Capillaries
D) Venules

The number of chambers in the human heart is:

A) Two
B) Three
C) Five
D) Four

The loss of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant is called:

A) Transpiration
B) Translocation
C) Guttation
D) Respiration

Water is absorbed from the soil mainly through the:

A) Stomata
B) Root hairs
C) Lenticels
D) Xylem vessels

The movement of manufactured food through the phloem is known as:

A) Transpiration
B) Transamination
C) Translocation
D) Transduction

Dissolved food substances, hormones and wastes are transported mainly in the:

A) Red blood cells
B) Platelets
C) White blood cells
D) Plasma

Human blood passes through the heart twice in one complete circuit; this is called:

A) Double circulation
B) Single circulation
C) Open circulation
D) Partial circulation

The valves in the heart and veins are important because they:

A) Pump the blood
B) Prevent the backflow of blood
C) Make new blood cells
D) Filter the blood
items.correct_answer: B) Prevent the backflow of blood

items.prompt:
The continuous upward movement of water in the xylem is helped by a force created by transpiration called the:

A) Root pressure only
B) Osmotic shock
C) Transpiration pull
D) Capillary fall

In humans, oxygenated blood is carried from the lungs to the heart by the:

A) Pulmonary artery
B) Vena cava
C) Hepatic vein
D) Pulmonary vein

The release of energy from food in living cells is called:

A) Respiration
B) Photosynthesis
C) Transpiration
D) Digestion

Respiration that requires oxygen and fully breaks down glucose is:

A) Anaerobic respiration
B) Aerobic respiration
C) Fermentation
D) Photosynthesis

Respiration that takes place in the absence of oxygen is described as:

A) Aerobic respiration
B) External respiration
C) Anaerobic respiration
D) Internal respiration

Most of the energy in cellular respiration is released in the:

A) Chloroplasts
B) Ribosomes
C) Nucleus
D) Mitochondria

The end products of complete aerobic respiration of glucose are:

A) Carbon dioxide and water
B) Glucose and oxygen
C) Alcohol and carbon dioxide
D) Lactic acid only

The energy released during respiration is stored in the cell as:

A) DNA
B) ATP
C) Starch
D) Chlorophyll

Anaerobic respiration in yeast produces ethanol (alcohol) and:

A) Oxygen
B) Water
C) Carbon dioxide
D) Lactic acid

Anaerobic respiration in human muscles during hard exercise produces:

A) Ethanol
B) Oxygen
C) Glucose
D) Lactic acid

mcq_options.text: Glucose + oxygen -> carbon dioxide + water + energy

items.prompt:
Which word equation correctly summarises aerobic respiration?

A) Glucose + oxygen -> carbon dioxide + water + energy
B) Carbon dioxide + water -> glucose + oxygen
C) Glucose -> ethanol + carbon dioxide + energy
D) Water + energy -> glucose + oxygen
items.correct_answer: A) Glucose + oxygen -> carbon dioxide + water + energy

items.prompt:
The physical movement of air into and out of the lungs is properly called:

A) Cellular respiration
B) Breathing (ventilation)
C) Photosynthesis
D) Transpiration

The gas taken in during human breathing for use in respiration is:

A) Carbon dioxide
B) Nitrogen
C) Oxygen
D) Hydrogen

The gas given out as a waste product of respiration during breathing is:

A) Oxygen
B) Nitrogen
C) Water vapour only
D) Carbon dioxide

In the human lungs, gaseous exchange takes place across the thin walls of the:

A) Alveoli (air sacs)
B) Bronchi
C) Trachea
D) Diaphragm

The breakdown of sugar by yeast to produce alcohol and carbon dioxide is used in baking and brewing and is called:

A) Respiration only
B) Fermentation
C) Digestion
D) Transpiration

The chemical used to confirm that exhaled air contains carbon dioxide is:

A) Iodine solution
B) Benedict's solution
C) Limewater
D) Hydrochloric acid

The dome-shaped muscle that flattens during inhalation to enlarge the chest cavity is the:

A) Intercostal cartilage
B) Epiglottis
C) Larynx
D) Diaphragm

mcq_options.text: Completely breaks down glucose to carbon dioxide and water

items.prompt:
Aerobic respiration releases more energy than anaerobic respiration because it:

A) Completely breaks down glucose to carbon dioxide and water
B) Uses no oxygen at all
C) Produces only lactic acid
D) Stops at ethanol
items.correct_answer: A) Completely breaks down glucose to carbon dioxide and water

items.prompt:
The extra oxygen needed after vigorous exercise to remove lactic acid is known as:

A) Oxygen tension
B) Oxygen debt
C) Oxygen saturation
D) Vital capacity

mcq_options.text: Thin-walled, moist and richly supplied with blood capillaries

items.prompt:
Alveoli are well adapted for gaseous exchange because they are:

A) Thick-walled and dry
B) Few and far apart
C) Thin-walled, moist and richly supplied with blood capillaries
D) Made of bone
items.correct_answer: C) Thin-walled, moist and richly supplied with blood capillaries

items.prompt:
During inhalation the volume of the chest cavity increases and the air pressure inside the lungs:

A) Increases, so air rushes out
B) Stays exactly the same
C) Becomes zero
D) Decreases, so air rushes in
items.correct_answer: D) Decreases, so air rushes in

items.prompt:
The removal of metabolic waste products from the body is called:

A) Excretion
B) Egestion
C) Secretion
D) Ingestion

The main organ of excretion in humans, which filters the blood, is the:

A) Liver
B) Kidney
C) Lung
D) Stomach

The chief nitrogenous waste product excreted in human urine is:

A) Glucose
B) Starch
C) Urea
D) Protein

The basic functional and filtering unit of the kidney is the:

A) Neuron
B) Alveolus
C) Villus
D) Nephron

mcq_options.text: Sweat containing water, salts and some urea

items.prompt:
Apart from temperature control, the skin also acts as an excretory organ by removing:

A) Sweat containing water, salts and some urea
B) Carbon dioxide only
C) Undigested food
D) Bile
items.correct_answer: A) Sweat containing water, salts and some urea

items.prompt:
The excretory waste products removed by the lungs are:

A) Urea and salts
B) Carbon dioxide and water vapour
C) Bile and faeces
D) Glucose and amino acids
items.correct_answer: B) Carbon dioxide and water vapour

items.prompt:
The tube that carries urine from each kidney to the bladder is the:

A) Urethra
B) Oviduct
C) Ureter
D) Vas deferens

Urine is temporarily stored before being passed out in the:

A) Gall bladder
B) Kidney
C) Ureter
D) Urinary bladder

The tube through which urine leaves the body from the bladder is the:

A) Urethra
B) Ureter
C) Oviduct
D) Bile duct

The liver contributes to excretion by producing bile pigments from the breakdown of:

A) Bone tissue
B) Worn-out red blood cells
C) Muscle protein only
D) Nerve cells

Sweat is produced and released onto the skin surface by the:

A) Sebaceous glands only
B) Hair follicles
C) Sweat glands
D) Nephrons

The knot of capillaries in the nephron where blood is filtered is the:

A) Glomerulus
B) Bowman's capsule only
C) Loop of Henle
D) Collecting duct

The first stage of urine formation, in which water and small molecules are forced out of the blood, is:

A) Reabsorption
B) Ultrafiltration
C) Secretion
D) Egestion

Useful substances such as glucose are returned to the blood in the kidney tubule during:

A) Filtration
B) Excretion
C) Selective reabsorption
D) Digestion

Plants get rid of excess water vapour mainly through:

mcq_options.text: Increase the organism's chance of survival and reproduction

items.prompt:
Adaptations are important to organisms because they:

items.correct_answer: A) Increase the organism's chance of survival and reproduction

mcq_options.text: The lower surface needs no gases
That is the only surface exposed to the air

items.prompt:
Floating water-lily leaves have their stomata on the upper surface because:

items.correct_answer: B) That is the only surface exposed to the air

mcq_options.text: Large, thin and well-supplied gill surface

items.prompt:
Fish gills are highly efficient at taking up oxygen partly because of a:

items.correct_answer: C) Large, thin and well-supplied gill surface
